Hi Tessa,

We had a sharp latency and error-rate spike on the checkout funnel this morning starting ~08:45 PT. Page loads for cart->checkout went from ~250ms median to 3-6s and we saw a burst of 5xx errors from tokenization/embedding calls. Impact: ~12% of live requests failed or timed out for ~20 minutes; peak throughput dropped by ~40%.

Attached is a zipped log bundle (novaline-logs-20270419.zip) with request traces, token-level timings, and a sample of failing request IDs.

Can you confirm if you saw capacity or model routing anomalies on your side? This is directly customer impacting and our ops/commerce team needs an immediate mitigation and an executive readout.

Thanks,

Subject: Internal: Novaline initial post-incident analysis and mitigations

Tessa/junior ops — summary from the bridge and my quick analysis:

What happened (short):
- A customer traffic pattern shift triggered a KV cache miss amplification for long-prefix streaming requests. The miss storm increased token generation latency and forced long-running in-flight batches.
- Simultaneous model-host contention occurred: a background GC-like spike on one host coincided with the cache misses and drove a cascade of request retries.

Immediate mitigations applied (timeline):
- 09:00: scaled Dedicated pool +20% (immediate capacity to clear backlog).
- 09:02: activated fallback routing to model-variant v2f (more conservative batching, slightly higher token cost but lower tail latency).
- 09:05: switched problematic host out of rotation and rebalanced KV shards.

Data / evidence:
- Increased 500-series from tokenization step (IDs in attached log bundle).
- CPU spikes and long GC pause on host gpu-78a (trace ids in mitigation_report.pdf).

Short-term gaps to remediate:
- Autoscaler had a conservative threshold for prefix-heavy workloads; it didn't react fast enough to sudden cache miss-driven latency.
- Host health signaling didn't capture GC-induced latency spikes as separate from application load.

Next steps (owners & ETA):
- Jordan: produce mitigation_report.pdf (attached) and confirm host replacement / kernel patch schedule by EOD.
- Karthik: audit autoscaler thresholds & recommend workload-specific rules (ETA 48h).
- Marissa: coordinate customer comms and formalize exec sync cadence (ETA 2h for draft email).

Evidence attachments: mitigation_report.pdf (short), host-traces.csv (referenced in PDF).

- Jordan
Sr. Incident Lead, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

Elena / Michael —

Thanks again for the quick coordination. Attached is the draft RCA and action plan (novaline-rca-draft.docx). High-level summary below; attachment contains timeline, root cause evidence, and a tracked list of corrective actions with owners and target dates.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Impact window: 2027-04-19 08:45–09:05 PT.
- User-facing effect: median checkout latency increased to 3–6s; ~12% error rate at peak; throughput reduced ~40%.
- Root cause: KV-cache miss amplification for long-prefix streaming requests plus a coincident host-level GC spike that caused request retries and head-of-line blocking.

Corrective actions (summary):
1) Immediate (complete): pool scale +20%, fallback routing to v2f, host replaced and KV shards rebalanced.
2) Near-term (2–7 days): autoscaler tuning for prefix-heavy traffic, per-workload scaling rules, enhanced host health metric (GC-latency alerting). Owner: karthik_iyer.
3) Mid-term (2–6 weeks): kernel-level runtime patch to reduce GC pause interaction with IO; improved prefix caching logic to avoid amplification. Owner: jordan_blake.
4) Customer comms & remediation: one-time usage credit to compensate partial downtime; postmortem call with your execs + monthly follow-up for 3 months. Owner: marissa_cole.

Requested exec ask: can we schedule a 30-min exec sync tomorrow (2027-04-23) to walk the RCA and confirm the remediation timeline and compensation? Proposed attendees: Elena, Michael, Tessa, Jordan, Karthik, Marissa.

Links and artifacts: RCA draft (attached), mitigation_report.pdf (from bridge), telemetry dashboard (link below).

I will not finalize the external postmortem until we get your input and sign-off on the compensation and timeline.

Appreciate your patience — we take this seriously and will share a tracked commitments CSV once targets are firmed.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Lead, Priority Customers
Redwood Inference
